newsitem.title: CHINA: China province plans for Taiwan phone, postal link.
newsitem.headline: China province plans for Taiwan phone, postal link.

text.p: China's southern province of Fujian has drawn up a plan for postal and telephone links with Taiwan once the island ends its ban on such links, the official Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
It quoted the director of the Fujian posts and telecommunications agency as saying a detailed draft had been made for links with the island across the Taiwan Strait.
"Post and telecom operations in Fujian... can be linked with their Taiwan counterparts just as soon as the time is right," the agency quoted Shangguan Qiwen as saying.

Taiwan has banned direct mail and telephone links -- as well as direct investment and trade -- since its Nationalist government fled to the island on its defeat by the communists in the Chinese civil war in 1949.

In recent years Fujian, China's closest province to Taiwan, has been a focus of indirect investment from the island and has been allowed to make the first tentative moves toward direct trade with the creation of a transshipment route.
Taiwan has rejected China's calls to abandon its ban on direct links, hoping to use this as a bargaining chip in its relations with Beijing, which views the island as a rebel province.
China held war games and missile tests off Taiwan's coast in a show of force in March last year, setting back efforts for a political accommodation between the two rival governments.
But the rapid growth in China's telecommunications sector has laid the foundation for future links with the island, Xinhua said.
Under the plan, the two sides could use microwave transmission or lay a submarine fibre optic cable between China's coastal city of Xiamen and the nearby Nationalist island of Quemoy, Xinhua said.

The Fujian cities of Fuzhou and Xiamen could be linked to Taipei by a domestic or international satellite, the agency said. A satellite ground station would be opened in Fuzhou later this year, it said.
Mail ships could sail between Fujian and Quemoy as well as Matsu, another Nationalist-held island, the news agency said.
